newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia trade unions to meet Monday on BHP Steel.
newsitem.headline: Australia trade unions to meet Monday on BHP Steel.

text.p: The Australian Council of Trade Unions (ACTU) said on Wednesday the union movement was extremely angry at the decision of The Broken Hill Pty Co (BHP) to end steel-making at Newcastle.
ACTU national affiliates would meet next Monday to consider any collective action which could be taken by the national trade union movement to ensure the job security of steel workers.
The ACTU statement did not say what collective action would be considered at Monday's meeting in Sydney.
But an ACTU spokesman told Reuters the meeting would take its direction from a mass meeting of workers at the Newcastle steelworks on Friday.
An Australian Workers' Union (AWU) official at Newcastle has already raised the prospect of an industrial campaign to block BHP's exports.
"What the members say on Friday will be extremely important," said ACTU senior industrial officer John Cairns.
